item.title: Pro tip: Screens hijack our nervous system
item.description: "Don't turn your phone on for at least the first hour you are awake," says Liz Roseman, an acupuncturist and life coach. "The screen hijacks our nervous system, essentially putting us into 'on/go' mode."

item.title: Letter: On board with making roads safer for cyclists
item.description: "I wholeheartedly agree that anything we can do to create a safer bicycle ride in the Asheville area is a step in the right direction."

item.title: Letter: Bikes and cars are incompatible on local roads
item.description: "If cyclists insist on traveling winding mountain roads, they either have to accept the endangerment or fund the creation of bike lanes."

item.title: Letter: Roads aren’t safe for bikes or cars
item.description: "Riding a bike in this area is like swimming in shark-infested waters."

item.title: Aspiring filmmaker seeks community stories about the opioid crisis
item.description: “This crisis is not only about drugs,” says James Walden. “It is about housing, mental health, poverty, trauma and the way our community responds to people in need. Fentanyl exposes every weakness in the system.”

item.title: What’s your take on Auggie the dachshund’s story? I beg to differ
item.description: Our columnists consider the saga of Auggie the dachshund — and freedom of expression in our area.

item.title: Western North Carolina homeowners eligible for federal funds for energy upgrades
item.description: Homeowners in Western North Carolina can receive thousands of dollars in federal funding for energy upgrades through the state-run Energy Saver North Carolina program, yet many eligible residents remain unaware of it.
